枕.meaning: A <part>sleeper</part> camping in the woods forgets her pillow, so she rests her head on a mossy root of a <part>tree</part>. The tree feels sorry for her and grows the moss thicker all night, soft as feathers. By dawn it's the comfiest <kanji>pillow</kanji> in the forest.
枕.on: She wakes up with moss stuck to her <sound>chin</sound>.
枕.kun: Her <sound>ma</sound>ma <sound>coo</sound>ks <sound>ra</sound>men for breakfast beside the tree.

搾.meaning: A sailor wants juice but has no press, so she jams an orange into a <part>hole</part> in the ship's <part>coat rack</part> and leans the iron <part>anchor</part> on top. Juice sprays everywhere, even into the parrot's eye. One mighty <kanji>squeeze</kanji>.
搾.on: She waters her potted <sound>suc</sound>culent with the drips.
搾.kun: <sound>She</sound> pours what's left into a <sound>bo</sound>ttle for the parrot.

諮.meaning: Before every <part>speech</part>, the mayor turns to the <part>next</part> seat, where her goldfish sits in its bowl. It opens its <part>mouth</part>: bloop. She nods and tears up page two. She never says a word in public without stopping to <kanji>consult with</kanji> the fish.
諮.on: When it disagrees, the goldfish hides behind a tiny knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
諮.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>! Stay <sound>ca</sound>lm,' it bloops, and the mayor breathes again.

愁.meaning: Every <part>autumn</part>, a scarecrow watches the leaves fall and the birds fly south without him. His straw <part>heart</part> sinks a little lower with each one that leaves. By November he droops on his pole, buttons sagging: the picture of <kanji>distress</kanji>.
愁.on: One crow flies back to cheer him up and leaves him a tiny <sound>shoe</sound>.
愁.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>h,' he moans, as a <sound>re</sound>d leaf lands on his nose.

汎.meaning: A chef makes one sauce for everything: <part>water drops</part>, salt and anything <part>commonplace</part> from the shelf. It goes on soup, cake, toast, even the cat's dinner. Never great, never bad, always there: her <kanji>general</kanji> sauce.
汎.on: One day she stirs in a spoon of <sound>hon</sound>ey and it's great on everything.
汎.kun: '<sound>Ta</sound>-<sound>da</sound>!' she sings, tipping a pot into the stream, and the sauce floats away <sound>yo</sound>nder: to drift.

遷.meaning: A zoo moves its reptile house <part>west</part>. A <part>large</part> basket with a <part>cobra</part> inside rolls up a <part>ramp</part> onto a train, and at every stop the cobra pokes its head out at the new view: desert, then hills, then sea. One long, slow <kanji>transition</kanji>.
遷.on: At the new zoo, a <sound>sen</sound>try checks the cobra's ticket.
遷.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>h,' says the cobra at the sea, then sneezes in the salty air: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

租.meaning: A guard on a bridge stops every cart of <part>grain</part> and takes one sack from the pile, and <part>moreover</part> one more sack for every layer stacked on top. The farmers grumble about it, but they pay the <kanji>tariff</kanji>.
租.on: He stacks the sacks into a lumpy <sound>so</sound>fa and naps on it.
